Stated Claim / Post Context:
Van Jones compares Republican midterm losses to mass murder-suicide at Jonestown

Van Jones likened the Republican Party's midterm election losses to the Jonestown mass murder-suicide, calling the results a full repudiation of President Donald Trump.

Actual Article Body:

Van Jones said he is "happy happy happy" over Republican defeats in the midterms, which he compared to the infamous cult mass murder-suicide at Jonestown.

CNN analyst Van Jones celebrated the Democrats’ midterm election victories Tuesday night by comparing the defeat for Republicans to the infamous 1978 Jonestown mass murder-suicide and calling the results a repudiation of President Donald Trump.

"I'm happy, happy, happy," Jones said of the election results. "I'm so happy. Listen, this is way bigger. This is like Christmas and a birthday and the Easter bunny and Halloween. This is the repudiation of Trumpism that people have been hoping for, seeing American democracy — seeing that sometimes you have kleptocratic rulers that get in power and ensconce themselves for decades in America. Twenty-four months later, 'Knock it off, we don’t want it.'"

He then compared the GOP losses to the mass murder-suicide at the Peoples Temple commune in Jonestown, Guyana, where more than 900 people died after cult leader Jim Jones directed his followers to drink cyanide-laced beverages.

"And by the way, if you join a cult at some point, the cult leader takes you to Jonestown and tries to get you to drink the Kool-aid. This is Jonestown for the Republican Party," he said. "They drank the Kool-Aid, and they have candidates that are dropping like flies across the country because they did not stand up to this guy when he was doing things that were wrong, when he was violating the law, when he was running over our system, they didn’t stand up to him, and they’re paying the price."

THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS IS JUST THE BEGINNING. HERE'S WHAT'S AT STAKE ON ELECTION DAY

Van Jones compared Republican losses in the 2026 midterms to the mass murder-suicide at Jonestown. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)

"It's Jonestown tonight," Jones added. "You join a cult, at some point, you go to Jonestown. That's where you are tonight, Republicans."

"Scott, I don't know if you want to check what's in your glass," CNN anchor Anderson Cooper then joked to Republican panelist Scott Jennings, who was sitting next to Jones.

"Do you realize I'm sitting right here? I can hear everything you're saying," Jennings said. "I've been here the entire time."

Jennings, however, acknowledged that Republicans were facing significant election losses.

"Well, look, I'm not going to sugarcoat it. There's a political science term for what's happening. It's called a country a-- whooping," he said. "That's what's happening right now. Across the board."

FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: AS THE HOUSE FALLS, THE SENATE STAYS IN PLAY

CNN commentator Scott Jennings said cost-of-living concerns and gas prices were key factors in Republican losses in the 2026 midterm elections. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

"There's a lot, a lot, a lot of reasons for what's happening right now," Jennings continued. "The most immediate issue is cost of living and gas prices. And that, that is the bottom line."

"You could read into a lot of other things," he added. "You can be jubilant about this, that or the other. But at the end of the day, the American people have here and now concerns. And that's really the lesson you got to take away from this."

Van Jones argued the midterm election results were a "repudiation of Trumpism." (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Republican Incumbent Vermont Gov. Phil Scott to Serve Sixth Term in Office

Incumbent Vermont Gov. Phil Scott (R) secured another term on Tuesday night in the state's 2026 gubernatorial election, NBC News projects.
The post Republican Incumbent Vermont Gov. Phil Scott to Serve Sixth Term in Office appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Incumbent Vermont Gov. Phil Scott (R) secured another term on Tuesday night in the state’s 2026 gubernatorial election, NBC News projects.

The governor’s race was called before 11 p.m. with most of the votes counted, showing Scott leading his opponent, Democrat Amanda Janoo, 52.1 percent to 46.2 percent.

Scott’s victory means he will serve a sixth term as Vermont governor, making him the longest-serving governor in the state’s history. In Vermont, there are no term limits, and governors serve two-year terms.

Scott’s challenger, Janoo, is a Strafford native who serves as the economics and policy lead for the Wellbeing Economy Alliance and worked as a financial adviser to the governments of Scotland, Wales, Finland, and New Zealand, among others.

While Scott identifies as a Republican, he has a history of being extremely socially liberal, which seems to allow him to dance a fine line in a deep blue state that has had a Democrat-dominated state Senate and House for two decades.

Some examples include him supporting allowing non-citizens across the state to vote in local municipality elections and being pro-abortion.

Katherine Hamilton is a political reporter for Breitbart News. You can follow her on X @thekat_hamilton.

[Source 3 — nypost.com (Bias: Right / Tabloid Conservative)] (URL: https://nypost.com/2026/11/04/us-news/cnns-van-jones-boasts-hes-happy-and-donald-trump-is-miserable-during-midterm-election-coverage/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
CNN’s Van Jones boasts he’s ‘happy and Donald Trump is miserable’ during midterm election coverage

“I’m happy Donald Trump is miserable and I’m happy tonight," Jones boasted.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Lefty CNN commentator Van Jones flaunted his glee over President Trump’s assumed misery following Democrats’ dramatic sweep of Congress during live election coverage Tuesday night.

“Can I be happy for my party?” Jones said during the network’s live rolling results coverage panel.

“I don’t want to talk about Donald Trump anymore,” he said.

Republican Scott Jennings was seated next to Jones and appeared to grow visibly irked as the lefty commentator continued his over-the-top victory lap.

Panelist Kasie Hunt interrupted by saying, “But they’re going to talk about Donald Trump,” before Jones went back to his bragging parade.

“I’m happy, you’re not going to steal my joy, I’m happy,” he boasted.

“Because the first gay man in the Senate, Chris Pappas of New Hampshire. We got a black female senator for the first time out of Illinois, Juliana Stratton. We got three black governors serving at the same time in America,” Jones said.

“We’re gonna have a black speaker of the House,” he added. “I’m happy Donald Trump is miserable and I’m happy tonight.”

Earlier in the night, Jennings squirmed as Jones broke out into sing-song speech, expressing his happiness over the Democratic wins.

CNN host Anderson Cooper asked Jones if the results were “bigger than you hoped for?” to which the Dem commentator gushed, “I’m happy, happy, happy! I’m so happy! Listen, this is way bigger.”

“This is like Christmas, and a birthday and the Easter Bunny, and Halloween. This is the repudiation of Trump-ism that people have been hoping for, seeing American democracy stand up,” he said.

At that point, a fed-up Jennings rolled his eyes at Jones.

“Sometimes you have kleptocratic rulers that get in power and they ensconce themselves for decades. In America, 24 months later, knock it off, you don’t want it,” Jones slamed.

While the results were still rolling in after midnight, the Democrats won control of the Senate and are projected to win in the House.
